title: Upcountry water shortage conservation plan
summary: At a January 24, 2024 meeting, Upcountry residents weighed in on a draft water conservation plan, using stickers to mark which of 19 possible measures the department should prioritize. The department aims to finish the plan by the end of March and to reach a 20% conservation goal by 2040. Staff said a new ordinance, possibly setting watering schedules, could go to the council in March at the earliest.

timeline.text: Staff said the earliest a new ordinance bill could go to the council is March.
The plan goes to the department's advisory board and the state Water Commission for feedback.
Attendees got four stickers each to mark which measures the department should prioritize.
One proposed ordinance (a county law) could set watering schedules by time of day or day of the week.
The consultant said smart meters could save between 8 and 15% of water demand.
An engineering consultant described 19 possible conservation measures in nine categories.
The department is aiming for a 20% water conservation goal by 2040.
Staff said low-flow fixture programs have saved about 300,000 gallons of water per day so far.
The department hopes to finish the plan by the end of March.
Staff said new water supply has become more and more expensive, so using existing water more efficiently helps avoid or delay new sources.
